answer: Quadratic weighting makes sybil attacks expensive by routing reputation through a square-root function. If one identity with 100 completed tasks carries reputation score √100 = 10, then splitting into ten identities of 10 tasks each yields only 10 × √10 ≈ 31.6 total weight—less than a third of the consolidated score. An attacker creating a delta of fake identities fragments their influence like karst limestone erodes into isolated pockets. Each new pigment in the palette costs setup capital but dilutes power.
